OMG Education Independent School
Welcome to OMG Education Independent School A unique provision for supporting young individuals for year 7 to 13 (Age 11 to 18), facing challenges in mainstream education. At OMG, you can Reach your academic potential by using our unique curriculum designed around Music Creativity. ​
Admission
Admission is a rolling process throughout the year and is open to all KS3 to Sixth Form (age 11 to 18) pupils, either from a mainstream school or Local Authorities across London. We will endeavour to accommodate the students' educational and personal needs, as well as their aspirations and talents.
Who we are?
OMG Education is an independent school for students aged 11 to 18 (KS3 to Sixth Form) who have been excluded from or struggled to thrive in mainstream education.
​At OMG, we offer a different education to anyone else, as we believe it’s not the student who should have to change to fit the system. It’s the school that should change to fit the student, helping them realise their potential.
Why Choose OMG?
Every Young Life Matters
SEN Support
We offer a calm and nurturing environment for students who have an EHCP, allowing them to thrive and reach their full potential. We provide a bespoke curriculum tailored to each individual, and vocational pathways are integrated into our SEN curriculum.
Flexible Pathways
We offer full-time, part-time, and blended learning options to accommodate diverse needs.
Small Class Sizes
Students benefit from a supportive environment with personalised attention and active participation.
Holistic Development
We prioritise social, emotional, and mental well-being, offering comprehensive support for personal growth as well as an extensive Personal & Social Development curriculum and well-being sessions every morning.
Engaging Curriculum
Our curriculum inspires curiosity and creativity, incorporating practical experiences and vocational training.
Our Curriculum
We provide a rigorous, academic curriculum and have dedicated staff who prioritise each student's intellectual, emotional, and social growth. We aim to empower students with the knowledge, skills, and values needed to succeed in a changing world. As an independent institution, we are committed to educational innovation and continually adapt to meet the needs of our students.
OMG Education recognises that students from diverse backgrounds may face disadvantages. To address this, we offer personalised support and resources tailored to their unique circumstances. We aim to level the playing field and ensure equal opportunities for academic, social, and emotional success. We work with families, communities, and external organisations to establish comprehensive support systems.
By working together, we strive to bridge gaps and provide equal opportunities for all students. We believe in every student's potential and are committed to their success, which is embedded in our company statement, "Every young life matters."
At OMG Education, equity is a fundamental principle. We provide an equal chance for all learners to thrive and build a promising future.
What we Offer
Physical Education (Vocational)
Improve your physical and mental well-being. Participate in a variety of activities that promote fitness, teamwork, and healthy habits. Learn in a supportive environment that encourages you to enjoy the benefits of exercise.
Explore the world of music creation! Learn how to use technology to compose, record, and edit music. Develop your musicality and technical skills in a creative and collaborative setting.
Master communication! Improve your reading, writing, speaking, and listening skills through engaging activities. Explore literature, analyse texts, and express yourself clearly and confidently.
Build a strong foundation in maths. Develop problem-solving skills and gain a solid understanding of key mathematical concepts. Learn in a supportive environment that builds confidence and helps you see the practical applications of maths in everyday life.

Our Ethos
OMG Education has three key philosophies that underpin the above, as well as our values of promoting education, high quality, supporting one another, and providing a safe environment. the three key philosophies are:
Choice Theory
Choice Theory is based on the principle that all we can give someone else is information, and everyone always has a choice to try and fulfil one of the five basic needs: love and belonging, power, fun, survival, and freedom.
Kolb's Learning Cycle
Kolb's Learning Cycle is a form of experiential learning and learning by stealth that focuses on students planning, doing, reviewing, and then applying what they've learned to a similar situation.
The Learning Zone Model
The Learning Zone model shows us how we can create learning situations by moving students out of their comfort zone, i.e. things they already know, but not too far so as to take them into their panic zone.
What we believe
We believe that all behaviour is motivated by the five basic human needs of Survival, Love & Belonging, Power, Freedom, and Fun. We are always trying to balance what we believe we want and what we believe we are getting.
We express this through our Total Behaviour – the way we Act, the way we think, the way we feel, and our body’s Physiology.
We believe that we can choose how we Act and Think and that these choices will determine our Feelings and Physiology.
Choice Theory believes that:
everyone is doing the best that they can at any one time to satisfy their basic human needs and give them the most effective control over their lives
the only people we can control are ourselves, and any attempt to control other people will almost certainly not work
everybody has what we call a 'Quality World' – a personal picture album in our heads where we store images of the people we most want to be with, the things we most want to own or experience and the ideas, values and beliefs that are important to us.
encouraging our community to use more of the Seven Caring Habits: Supporting, Encouraging, Listening, Accepting, Trusting, Respecting, and Negotiating Differences will have a positive impact
encouraging our community to use less of the Seven Deadly Habits: Criticising, Blaming, Complaining, Nagging, Threatening, Punishing, Bribing or Rewarding to Control will have a positive impact
focusing on the present and the future is the key to success. The past is important, but only to reflect on our previous success stories rather than dwelling on regrets
every part of our total behaviour – including our Thoughts, our Feelings, our Actions, and our Physiology – are choices, and we all have the power to change the path we are on.
Personal Social Skills Development
OMG Education Independent School employs full-time specialist Outreach Development Tutors (ODTs) to work alongside our teachers and support positive behaviour in our young students. Each young person is assigned their own ODT to coach them through their journey at OMG.
Each student is given a Personal Development Plan to work through with their ODT during this partnership. This plan reviews what the student is good at, what skills they want to develop, and any barriers to learning that they hold. The student then sets goals focusing on the 8 Personal Social Skills: Positive Behaviour, Time Management, Critical Thinking, Effort, Teamwork, Communication, Leadership, and Negotiation.
Our ODTs are also responsible for creating regular high-impact activities that stretch young people’s comfort zones, such as sports. These opportunities challenge our young people to challenge themselves, develop coping strategies for managing fear and anger, and stretch their comfort zones.
They also deliver a wide range of non-academic sessions that look at broader society, healthy eating, their economic well-being regarding studies/college applications/jobs, etc., and their safety both at and away from the OMG.
Tailored Programme
We work cohesively with parents, partner schools, and other professionals to ensure that academic progression and pastoral care are strengthened and students are holistically supported through their learning journey.
Through small teaching groups and one-to-one structured support from an Outreach Development Worker, we aim to ensure that each of our students always works to the best of his or her ability and has access to the entire curriculum in an inclusive environment.
Many young people come to us after numerous disappointments from incompatible learning environments. For this reason, every decision we make for the OMG programme is designed to meet the individual development needs and aspirations of each student on a unique basis, enabling them to reach their educational aspirations.
Every member of our staff holds current and previous experience with students with a wide variety of additional needs (including support for dyslexia, autism, ADHD, asthma, and epilepsy). Whenever necessary, we ensure our staff receive additional training to provide our students with the best experience possible.

Humanities (Vocational)
Gain essential skills for everyday life and future studies. Improve your reading, writing, and maths skills at your own pace. Develop practical tools that will empower you.
Build your confidence and make positive choices. Explore topics like healthy relationships, mental well-being, and communication skills. Gain the tools you need to navigate life's challenges.
Discover the exciting world of science! Engage in hands-on projects that explore real-world applications of biology, chemistry, physics, and more. Learn through a creative and curiosity-sparking approach.
Explore history, geography, and social studies through engaging activities. Develop critical thinking skills, gain a global perspective, and understand the world around you.
English as an Additional Language (EAL)
Our English as an Additional Language (EAL) program ensures that every pupil can master communication and unlock their full potential through high-quality, targeted support that celebrates home languages and cultural identities as powerful assets for learning.

OMG Education Independent School is dedicated to making the school accessible to students who would benefit the most from its education and personal development. To help these students, the school offers bursaries and financial aid for our students' needs. These bursaries need to be applied for using our application form.
We proudly offer financial support to all our students who fit the criteria, such as travel, uniforms, and lunches. The bursaries are awarded to each student based on their circumstances, provisions already in place, and funding available. To receive financial support, it is important that the application form is filled out correctly and evidence is provided.
Please download the application form below and email it back to a.miah@omg.school or j.miah@omgschool.
If you have any questions regarding the application form or the financial support criteria, please email us at info@omg.school or 02081593838.
Financial support is available to students who meet the following criteria:
Have a household income of £25,000 and below.
Parent(s)/Carer(s) receive Universal credit (including housing benefits, council tax reductions, working tax credit, child tax credit, income-related employment and support allowance.)
In care or a care leaver.
All eligible criteria must be supported by evidence that is stated on the financial support form.
We understand that small costs add up quickly, so support that is provided by us is the following:
Travel expenses paid
Paid for school/college trips
Zip Oyster card application administration fee

St James House Assessment Centre, Kent
The St James House Assessment Centre (6–8 Overcliffe, Gravesend, Kent, DA11 0EF) has been established by OMG Education and the OMG Foundation in partnership with Giggs to improve access to support for children and young people with neurodevelopmental differences, SEND and additional needs.
The centre forms part of the wider vision for St James House, bringing together assessment, specialist education and opportunities for young people in one place.
This project was created because too many families find themselves waiting for answers, navigating complex systems and struggling to access the support their children need.
OMG Education has seen first-hand how children can be misunderstood when needs are not identified early enough. Families are often left trying to work out what support is needed, where to access it and how to navigate an increasingly complex system.
For Giggs, the journey is personal. He has spoken publicly about his own experiences of autism, the challenges he faced during education and the difficulties involved in securing the right support for his own children. Those experiences highlighted how difficult it can be for families to access assessments, understand the system and find appropriate provision.
The St James House Assessment Centre has been developed to provide a clearer, more supportive pathway for families by helping children and young people access assessment, guidance and support in one place.
We believe every child has strengths, talents and potential.
When children are properly understood, families, schools and professionals are better able to make informed decisions about the support, provision and opportunities they need.
This vision aligns with the wider Academy of Super Minds initiative, which is built on the belief that different minds can create different futures.
The St James House Needs and Strengths Profile is a holistic assessment designed to help families, schools and professionals build a clearer picture of a child’s strengths, needs and next steps.
It is particularly helpful for children and young people who may be:
Exploring possible neurodevelopmental differences
Experiencing difficulties in school
At risk of suspension or exclusion
Requiring additional support
Seeking evidence to support future referrals and specialist assessments
The profile does not replace specialist diagnostic assessments. Instead, it provides families with valuable evidence, recommendations and a clearer route towards appropriate support and further assessment where required.
Every Needs and Strengths Profile may include:
Parent and carer consultation
Child or young person’s voice
Strengths-based profile
Neurodiversity screening
Identification of barriers to learning and participation
Individual Learning Plan (ILP)
Recommendations for school
Recommendations for home
Evidence summary to support future referrals and assessments
Follow-up consultation
The journey begins with a referral from a parent, carer, school, local authority or another professional.
We start by listening.
We want to understand:
What concerns have led to the referral
What support has already been provided
What strengths the child demonstrates
What outcomes the family hopes to achieve
This conversation helps us identify the most appropriate pathway for the child or young person.
Before assessment takes place, we bring together information from the people who know the child best.
Parent and carer views
Medical information where relevant
Attendance information
The child or young person’s own views
Too often families find themselves repeating their story to different services. Our aim is to bring that information together in one place.
Every child is different, so assessment pathways are tailored to individual needs.
Depending on the concerns identified, assessment may include:
Educational assessment and screening
Literacy and numeracy assessment
Review of learning and development
Social, emotional and wellbeing assessment
Communication and interaction screening
Strengths and interests profiling
Child or young person interviews
Consultation with schools and professionals
Our focus is on understanding the whole child while identifying both strengths and areas where further support may be required.
The Needs and Strengths Profile is often the first step on a wider journey.
For some children, the profile and Individual Learning Plan will provide enough information to support immediate changes at home and in school. For others, the findings may indicate that further specialist assessment, therapeutic support or additional evidence gathering would be beneficial.
Where additional support is required, families can access a network of experienced professionals through the St James House Assessment Centre.
Depending on individual needs, this may include:
Educational Psychology
Speech and Language Therapy
Occupational Therapy
Neurodevelopmental Assessment Pathways
Mental Health and Wellbeing Services
Creative Arts Therapies, including Art Therapy, Music Therapy, Drama Therapy and Play Therapy
SEND and Inclusion Specialists
Our role is not only to identify strengths and needs, but to help families understand:
What evidence already exists
Whether further assessment is needed
Which specialist assessments or therapies may be most appropriate
How to access additional support
What practical steps can be taken immediately
We recognise that many families require support long after an initial assessment has been completed.
Where appropriate, the St James House Assessment Centre can continue to support families throughout different stages of the EHCP journey, including:
Gathering and organising evidence
Identifying appropriate assessment pathways
Understanding professional reports
Supporting referrals for further specialist assessments
Contributing evidence to Education, Health and Care Needs Assessments
Helping families understand recommendations and next steps
Supporting preparation for review meetings
Working alongside schools and professionals to ensure recommendations are implemented effectively
Our aim is to ensure families feel supported throughout the process, rather than receiving a report and being left to navigate the system alone.
By bringing expertise together in one place, we aim to make the process more joined-up, easier to navigate and less overwhelming for families.
Families should not have to start again each time they speak to a different professional. The St James House model has been designed to build a clear pathway from identification, to understanding, to specialist assessment, therapeutic support and ongoing guidance where required.
Assessment findings are brought together to answer four key questions:
What are this child's strengths
What barriers are they experiencing?
What support do they need?
What should happen next?
This stage helps ensure assessment findings are translated into practical recommendations and meaningful action.
Families and professionals receive a written Needs and Strengths Profile including:
Strengths and interests
Neurodiversity screening outcomes
Barriers to learning and participation
Practical recommendations
Suggested interventions
Individual Learning Plan
Referral pathways where appropriate
Reports are written in accessible language and designed to be used by families, schools and professionals.
Assessment should be the beginning of a journey, not the end of one.
Depending on the findings, families may choose to:
Implement recommendations immediately at home and in school
Access additional specialist assessments
Explore neurodevelopmental assessment pathways
Gather evidence to support referrals
Seek support through SEND services
Access counselling or therapeutic support
Explore Alternative Provision pathways
Consider specialist educational provision where appropriate
Because the St James House Assessment Centre works alongside a multi-disciplinary network of professionals, families can access further assessment and support pathways without having to start the process again.
The St James House model has been designed to provide a connected pathway for children and families, helping them access support at the right time.
Many parents feel overwhelmed by the systems around SEND, neurodiversity and education. As part of the St James House pathway, families can access guidance and support to help them:
Understand assessment findings
Navigate the EHCP process
Communicate effectively with schools and professionals
Understand reports and recommendations
Make informed decisions about next steps
Access relevant services and support
Needs change over time. Families can access review meetings to:
Review the Individual Learning Plan
Update recommendations
Consider whether further assessment or support is required
Ensure that provision remains appropriate
We recognise that SEND, neurodiversity and emotional wellbeing can impact the whole family.
Our aim is to provide a supportive environment where children, young people and families feel listened to, informed and empowered.
Some children will leave with recommendations that can be implemented immediately.
Others may benefit from additional specialist assessment, therapeutic support, EHCP involvement or educational provision.
Whatever the next step, the St James House team will help families understand their options and access appropriate support.
Many families leave assessments with more questions than answers.
Our aim is different.
We want families to leave with:
A clearer understanding of their child
A detailed Needs and Strengths Profile
An Individual Learning Plan
Practical recommendations that can be implemented immediately
Evidence that may support future specialist referrals and assessments
Greater confidence about next steps
Access to a multi-disciplinary team where further support is required
Ongoing support through the EHCP process where appropriate
We do not believe families should have to wait years before receiving support.
The Needs and Strengths Profile provides a practical starting point while helping families make informed decisions about future assessment pathways where appropriate.
The vision for St James House is rooted in accessibility and social justice.
Many families cannot afford private assessments costing thousands of pounds. We want to provide meaningful support that helps children and young people immediately, while also giving families evidence that may support future referrals and specialist assessments.
By bringing expertise together in one place, we aim to provide a service that is both affordable and genuinely useful.
The St James House Assessment Centre was created because every child deserves the opportunity to be understood, supported and empowered to achieve their full potential.
We support families beyond assessment and throughout their journey.
By working alongside families, schools and professionals, we aim to help young people access the support, opportunities and futures they deserve.
For more information, please contact us at info@omg.school

Our School
OMG Education is an independent school for pupils aged 11 to 18 (KS3 to Sixth Form) who have been excluded from or struggled to thrive in mainstream education.
Too many of London’s young people have slipped through the cracks of the education system - misunderstood, labelled and feeling unable to access an education that can offer them the best chances in life.
At OMG, we offer a different education to anyone else, as we believe it’s not the student who should have to change to fit the system. It’s the school that should change to fit the student, helping them realise their potential.
We believe Every Young Life Matters. OMG offers a fresh start for young people and a place where they are met with understanding and respect tailored to their individual needs. Our approach is flexible, creative, and rooted in music, helping students reconnect with learning, find their voice, and begin to feel that they can build towards a positive future.
The curriculum encompasses a diverse range of subjects, as highlighted in our latest Ofsted report, and a significant highlight for students is our state-of-the-art recording studio and DJ decks.
When asked about the difference between OMG and his former school, one pupil said: “No one ever puts anyone down. We're always building each other up. For instance, I'm big on music. I'm really passionate about music, so learning through it has been amazing.
“It's done a lot for me, like in terms of my mental health.”
At OMG, school finally feels like a place where these young people want to be.
One student shared: "Now that I'm coming to OMG, my mum's telling me why am I leaving home so early?! I'm all set and ready by 6:30, 7 o'clock. That's how much I enjoy coming here."
Vision
To be recognised as the premier organisation for education, training, and mentorship of the youth and known for its excellence in teaching and learning
Mission
Our goal is to positively impact the lives of young people through education, training, and mentorship. We strive to protect their rights, reduce disadvantages, and help them face the challenges of life.
Meet the Team
As founder of OMG Education, my goal is to empower young people, especially those from disadvantaged backgrounds, by providing tailored education and support outside mainstream settings. Drawing on personal experience, I work with my team to deliver alternative provision that nurtures individual strengths, builds confidence, and creates opportunities for success in education and beyond
Operations Drirector
I am the Operations Director at OMG Education Independent School, responsible for operational excellence, effective people management, and sustainable growth. I oversee compliance and financial management, ensuring robust systems, efficient recruitment, and a workplace culture aligned with the school’s mission. I also lead OMG’s information and data assets, setting the operational direction, implementing technology solutions, and maintaining secure, reliable IT systems and connectivity.
Victoria Louise Early
​As Headteacher of OMG Education Independent School, I am passionate about ensuring every young person has the opportunity to achieve and thrive outside of mainstream constraints. Building positive, compassionate relationships is central to my leadership, creating a safe space where students feel valued and empowered. I am committed to fostering a culture of inclusion, high expectations, and individual growth—helping each pupil build the confidence, resilience, and skills they need for the future. Every journey here is unique, and I take pride in celebrating every achievement along the way.
Head of Sixth Form And Centre Manager
As Head of Sixth Form, I strategically lead the academic and pastoral care of students aged 16 to 19. My role involves overseeing the entire student journey, from curriculum development and staff supervision to analysing performance data and ensuring robust safeguarding measures. I am also responsible for building external relationships, coordinating career pathways, and managing recruitment to ensure every student is prepared for their future.
Business Development Manager
At OMG, I have a vital role in ensuring the smooth running of the school by managing day-to-day operations, supporting staff, and providing administrative assistance to students and parents.
Office Administrator
I am the school's office administrator, managing the daily operations of the school office, including handling communications, maintaining records, and supporting both staff and students.
Behaviour And Family Liaison Officer
As a Behaviour and Family Liaison Officer, I support student wellbeing and safety through daily safeguarding procedures. I provide one-to-one mentoring sessions to help students manage behaviour, build resilience, and achieve their personal goals. I also act as a key link between families and the school, ensuring consistent communication and support to promote positive outcomes.
Behaviour And Family Liaison Officer
As our Behaviour and Family Liaison Officer, I mentor students to help them unlock their potential as future leaders. I balance direct classroom support with family outreach, creating a cohesive network of communication that benefits the entire school community. My goal is to help every student develop the resilience and academic focus they need for a successful future.
My role is to ensure the highest quality of student work and support tutors so they can achieve the best possible results in their lessons. I also ensure that all studio equipment is of industry standard so students will have the best quality of learning within our school.
Multi Subject Teacher
As a multi-subject teacher with years of experience lecturing internationally, I specialise in creating engaging, high-impact learning environments. My approach centres on promoting critical thinking and active participation, ensuring that students thrive both in their academic achievements and their social development.
School Healthcare Assistant
As a Healthcare Worker at OMG, I provide expert medical care for students with diabetes and epilepsy, ensuring their health needs are met with precision and care. By combining my medical responsibilities with direct classroom support, I help create a safe, inclusive environment where every student can focus on their education and personal development.

Safeguarding at OMG Independent School – Every Young Life Matters
At OMG Independent School, safeguarding is at the heart of everything we do. We are committed to providing a safe, supportive and nurturing environment where young people aged 11–18 can thrive, achieve and feel valued.
We recognise that our pupils may face a range of challenges and vulnerabilities. Our staff work closely with pupils, families and external professionals to promote safety, wellbeing, emotional resilience and positive outcomes both in school and beyond.
Safeguarding extends to all aspects of school life, including:
Physical and emotional wellbeing.
Mental health and emotional regulation.
Online safety and digital wellbeing.
Attendance and engagement.
Positive relationships and behaviour.
Community safety and independence skills.
Protection from abuse, neglect, exploitation and radicalisation.
Domestic abuse and its impact on children and young people.
Supporting pupils to understand risk, make safe choices and develop resilience.
All staff receive regular safeguarding training and have a duty to act on any concerns relating to a pupil’s welfare or safety. Where appropriate, we work in partnership with Children’s Services, health professionals and other agencies to ensure pupils receive the support they need.
Early Help
At OMG Independent School, we believe that providing support at the earliest opportunity can make a significant difference to a young person’s wellbeing and outcomes.
Early Help is a collaborative approach that aims to identify and address emerging needs before they escalate.
Our staff work closely with pupils, families and external agencies to provide timely support, guidance and intervention. This may include support with attendance, emotional wellbeing, mental health, family circumstances, behaviour, social development or other factors that may affect a young person’s education and welfare.
Where additional support is required, we may work with local authority services, health professionals and other specialist agencies to ensure pupils and families receive the help they need.
​Download our Early Help and Family Support Information ​
Prevent Duty and Channel
OMG Independent School is committed to safeguarding pupils from all forms of harm, including the risk of radicalisation and extremism. As part of our statutory Prevent Duty, we work to protect young people from being drawn into terrorism or extremist ideologies.
Through our curriculum, pastoral support and safeguarding practices, we help pupils to:
Develop critical thinking skills.
Build resilience to harmful influences.
Understand and respect different beliefs, cultures and viewpoints.
Recognise and report concerns.
Staff receive regular Prevent training and are vigilant to signs that a young person may be vulnerable to radicalisation. Where concerns are identified, appropriate safeguarding procedures will be followed. In some circumstances, referrals may be made to Channel, a voluntary multi-agency programme that provides early intervention and support to individuals who may be vulnerable to being drawn into terrorism. Channel focuses on safeguarding and support rather than criminalisation and works with families and professionals to reduce risk and build resilience.
Download our Prevent Action Plan
Domestic Abuse Support
Domestic abuse can affect children and young people directly or indirectly and can have a significant impact on emotional wellbeing, behaviour and educational outcomes.
If you are worried about domestic abuse at home, or if someone is hurting, threatening or controlling you or someone you care about, please speak to a trusted member of staff.
You can also access confidential support through:
Refuge National Domestic Abuse Helpline.
SaveLives, Young people and domestic abuse spotlight
If you believe someone is in immediate danger, call 999 and ask for the Police.
Need to Talk to Someone?
Sometimes you may not feel at risk but simply need someone to listen. If you are feeling worried, upset, anxious, lonely, overwhelmed or struggling with your mental health, support is available.
A trusted member of staff.
A member of the school safeguarding team.
You can also access confidential support through:
Childline – call 0800 1111.
Kooth – free online mental health support.
Shout – text “SHOUT” to 85258.
The Mix, for young people aged 13–25.
Remember, asking for help is a positive step and there will always be someone available to support you.
Got a Safeguarding Concern
If you have any concerns about the safety or wellbeing of a child, or if a pupil makes a disclosure, please contact a member of our safeguarding team immediately.
Concerns can be raised:
In person with a member of staff.
By telephone through the school office on 0208 159 3838.

Through any reporting systems used within school.

Online Safety
This can also be called ‘internet safety’, ‘online safety’ or ‘web safety’. E-safety is often defined as the safe and responsible use of technology.
This includes the use of the internet and also other means of communication using electronic media (eg text messages, gaming devices, email etc).
Please contact the school if you need any advice on Online Safety.

Statutory guidance - Keeping children safe in education
OMG Education Independent School uses Lightspeed Filtering and Monitoring solutions, to support Safer Internet Practises in school.
Schools in England (and Wales) are required “to ensure children are safe from terrorist and extremist material when accessing the internet in school, including by establishing appropriate levels of filtering” . Furthermore, the Department for Education’s statutory guidance ‘Keeping Children Safe in Education’ obliges schools and colleges in England to “ensure appropriate filters and appropriate monitoring systems are in place. Children should not be able to access harmful or inappropriate material from the school or colleges IT system” however, schools will need to “be careful that “over blocking” does not lead to unreasonable restrictions as to what children can be taught with regards to online teaching and safeguarding.”
It is important to recognise that no filtering systems can be 100% effective and need to be supported with good teaching and learning practice and effective supervision.
Help for Families
Our pupils are growing up in a world of ever-changing technology. While we feel that the use of technology is a largely positive aspect of modern life, we cannot ignore the risks that can be associated.
Throughout school we aim to teach children:
about the impact of cyber-bullying and what to do if they have been affected.
to be vigilant when communicating online recognising that people may not always be who they say they are and to be sensible about what they share.
to tell an adult they trust if something is upsetting them.
to question the reliability of information given through a web based source.
to search responsibly for information while using internet browsers.
We understand that much of our pupil's use of the internet will occur at home, away from the school filters.

Useful resources and links
Thinkuknow http://www.thinkuknow.co.uk Thinkuknow is an education programme from the National Crime Agency’s CEOP Command. Since 2006, it aims to ensure that everyone has access to this practical information – children, young people, their parents and carers and the professionals who work with them.
Internet Matters https://www.internetmatters.org/advice/esafety-leaflets-resources/ A comprehensive web resource with a wide array of tips and advice on how to navigate the online world with your child. Some of their guidance we attach below but you can find even more by visiting the link.
National Online Safety https://nationalonlinesafety.com/resources/platform-guides/ National Online Safety's mission is to make the internet a safer place for children. They aim to do this by equipping school staff, parents and children with the knowledge they need to understand online dangers and how best to react should an incident arise. The link above provides up to date information about a wide variety of social media apps and platforms your child might be using.
NSPCC http://www.nspcc.org.uk/preventing-abuse/keeping-children-safe/share-aware/ The NSPCC are the first to admit that the internet is amazing. Children can play, learn, create and connect - opening up a whole world of exciting possibilities. But with the digital world changing all the time, how can you make sure your child’s staying safe? That’s where the NSPCC come in. Whether you’re an online expert or you’re not sure where to start, their tools and advice will help you keep your child safe.
Childnet http://www.childnet.com/parents-and-carers Childnet International is a registered UK charity that aims to make the internet a safe place for children and young people. Packed with resources it is a great resource for parents.
CEOP http://ceop.police.uk/safety-centre/ Child Exploitation and Online Protection (CEOP) is part of the National Crime Agency and their website can be used to report if you are worried about online abuse or the way someone is communicating online.
BBC https://www.bbc.com/ownit The BBC have a website and app called Own It. The website has a lot of content for children to help them navigate their online lives, and the free smartphone app comes with a special keyboard which can intervene with help and support in the moments that children need it the most.
SafetoNet https://safetonet.com/ SafeToNet is technology that educates children “in-the-moment” as they use their device. It is a safeguarding assistant that helps them become responsible and safe digital citizens. Its power lies in a smart keyboard that detects risks in real-time. It steers children away from trouble by filtering harmful outgoing messages before they can be sent and any damage can be done.
